scope: Independent content review of the 98 official skills, course core and advanced lessons, official domain and scope snapshots, and repository inventory.
limits: Course material is broad and useful, but ID mapping does not prove substantive coverage.
AWS states its service list is non-exhaustive and subject to change. This review cannot certify undisclosed exam coverage.
No claim of exhaustive exam coverage is warranted.

findings.finding: Core lessons mention server-derived tenant filters, but need a worked identity-to-document authorization path, deny behavior, and cross-tenant negative cases. Skill 1.4.2 and 1.5.6 require substantive data integration and retrieval access design.
findings.recommendation: Add a case that follows authenticated identity through authorization, retrieval filtering, prompt construction, and negative tests.

findings.finding: Core-024 mentions stale vectors and cached responses, but it does not fully teach how deletion reaches queues, indexes, summaries, logs, and backups.
findings.recommendation: Teach source identifiers, versioned deletion events, retry tracking, derived data, and retention boundaries.

findings.finding: Core-038 and core-039 cover approval and tool contracts. A stronger worked case should bind approval to exact parameters, revalidate at execution, and use idempotency after retries.
findings.recommendation: Add a changed-parameter approval trap and walk the boundary from model proposal to server-side execution.

findings.finding: Core and advanced lessons correctly separate untrusted evidence and controls. Ensure diagrams never imply that delimiters or guardrails alone enforce tool authorization.
findings.recommendation: Label prompt boundaries as model guidance and label IAM plus server validation as enforcement.

findings.finding: Core-063 states AWS provider access and data terms. This is a time-sensitive service claim. The lesson correctly says to review current terms, but it should cite the dated official source snapshot and distinguish account access from retention and abuse detection settings.
findings.recommendation: Keep the statement bounded to the cited terms and review it before each course release.

findings.finding: The core introduces capacity, provisioned modes, batching, and quota distinctions. Add a worked peak-load case that keeps token rate, request rate, concurrency, quota, and price separate.
findings.recommendation: Use a sourced, model-specific example only when current quota and pricing evidence exists.

findings.finding: Core-026 says to use compatible document and query settings. It should explicitly treat model, dimension, normalization, and index migration as a versioned contract.
findings.recommendation: Teach blue-green index creation, retrieval evaluation, traffic switch, and rollback.

findings.finding: Core-019 lists extraction services and automation. It has limited instruction on extraction confidence, missing content, file validation, and stage-level diagnosis.
findings.recommendation: Add a document case where source, extraction, and prompt failures have distinct evidence.

findings.finding: Evaluation lessons cover metrics, judges, feedback, and rollout. A case should show judge calibration against human labels, pair order bias, and segment-level failure.
findings.recommendation: Add a small judge calibration exercise and require a disagreement review.

findings.finding: Core-050 and core-051 cover streaming and retry behavior. Add a single end-to-end deadline budget across retrieval, reranking, inference, tools, retries, and client disconnect.
findings.recommendation: Use a sequence diagram with explicit timeout ownership and partial response states.

findings.finding: Core-076 distinguishes audit activity from invocation logging. Add a clear evidence map that distinguishes identity and API events from supported prompt and response payload logs.
findings.recommendation: Show configuration, access restriction, retention, redaction, and supported-service limits.

findings.finding: Skill map lists all 98 IDs. Several skills have one mapped slide and terse bullets. Mapping alone cannot establish that examples, decision rules, and limits teach the full skill.
findings.recommendation: Score each official skill for concept, decision, worked case, failure mode, and source evidence. Mark weak coverage for targeted expansion.

findings.finding: The repository contains many custom and Mermaid SVG files. SVG visuals can oversimplify policy boundaries, imply unsupported guarantees, or render text inconsistently. Inventory alone cannot establish their semantic accuracy.
findings.recommendation: Review each published SVG against its lesson text and source. Check labels, arrows, alternate text, color contrast, and text rendering.

findings.finding: The course has scope snapshots and several current service documents. AWS marks in-scope services non-exhaustive and subject to change. Product feature details can also change.
findings.recommendation: Keep scope claims tied to the retrieved official snapshot and add a source review date to course maintenance records.

source_check.official_domains: The five domain snapshots enumerate all 98 skill statements and support the course domain labels.
source_check.scope: The official service scope snapshot explicitly says its list is non-exhaustive and subject to change.
source_check.citations: New lesson suggestions cite local MCP document stems. Verify every stem exists before merge.
source_check.source_claims: The audit did not re-fetch live AWS pages. It reviewed saved MCP snapshots only.

evidence_path_validation.correction: The out-of-scope snapshot is at research/aip-01-out-of-scope-services.md. The policies SVG cited in the review is in source-repo/assets/img/custom/.
evidence_path_validation.source_repo_limit: Inherited material was inventoried. It was not independently fact-verified.
